scope: Independent mechanical check of the current root-fixed cumulative RAFT inventory; direct relationship rows and accepted primary ledgers only.
method: Built inventory in memory with scripts/raft_export_inventory.py; compared direct rows to accepted primary direct_reply_pairs, recursively checked multi-ID fields and scope/date keys, and inspected legacy graph section rows. No inventory or script writes.

findings.finding: Current in-memory inventory matches root expected 221 direct edges and 205 unique outgoing Darwin responses.
No accepted direct pair uses incoming_ids or outgoing_ids arrays with more than one element; the generic next-first normalization has no observed multi-ID case to collapse.

Scope fields are optional per accepted record. The normalizer carries every populated response_scope/response_sections/response_paragraphs/response_fragments field; records with none are legacy or whole-body cases and require their existing accepted disposition, not invented paragraph ranges.

The 221 direct edges collapse to 205 responses because 16 outputs have multiple accepted incoming/scoped edges. They must remain one response unit with all incoming scopes retained, not 221 duplicated answers.

24 legacy 1837–1843 graph rows are classified direct by the root-fixed normalizer. Their graph edge direction is source incoming -> target Darwin response; retain graph provenance and do not reinterpret correspondent reverse replies as Darwin answers.

limitations: This is mechanical integrity/navigation evidence, not historical adjudication.
The root-fixed inventory counts are authoritative only after root regenerates and reviews the final scope matrix; the prior 196-row candidate is stale and excluded.
